extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (agents/attorneys), and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality/technical requirements for inventor oaths/declarations, inventor bibliographic information, signatures, identification of the application, joint inventorship, corrections, and supplemental oaths in U.S. patent applications (per MPEP §§602–603 and cited 37 CFR provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath or Declaration in Continuing Applications Filed Before September 16, 2012
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional application filed before September 16, 2012 under 37 CFR 1.53(b) (other than a continuation-in-part (CIP)) may be filed with a copy of the oath or declaration from the prior nonprovisional application. See pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.63(d)(1)(iv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a copy of a prior oath/declaration omits an inventor's signature, OPAP should send a Notice to File Missing Parts requiring the missing signature unless a copy of the decision according pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.47 status is included. Reply by filing a copy of the decision with a surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) for late filing is acceptable; alternatively submit the missing inventor's executed oath/declaration with the surcharge. If an inventor named in the prior application is not an inventor in the continuation/divisional, the continuation/divisional may be filed (A) with a copy of the prior oath/declaration plus a statement requesting deletion of the non‑inventor(s) (pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.63(d)), or (B) with a newly executed oath/declaration naming the correct inventive entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑English Oath or Declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an individual making an oath or declaration cannot understand English, the oath or declaration must be in a language that such individual can understand and shall state that such individual understands the content of any documents to which the oath or declaration relates (37 CFR 1.69).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless the text is in a PTO-provided form or conforms to PCT Rule 4.17(iv), a non-English oath/declaration must be accompanied by an English translation and a statement that the translation is accurate; for an oath/declaration filed under §1.63 the translation may be filed up to two months after applicant is notified to file it. A single non-English oath/declaration is acceptable where joint inventors all understand that non-English language. If documents are in a language the inventor cannot comprehend, they may be explained to the inventor so they understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Inventor and Application Information in Oath/Declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor’s oath or declaration must include certain inventor bibliographic information, name the inventor or each joint inventor and except as otherwise provided be signed by each inventor, and identify the application to which it is directed (see MPEP §602.08 and 37 CFR 1.63).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See subsections for specifics: inventor citizenship/residence/mail address, legal name rules, signature requirements, and acceptable methods to identify the application (e.g., name + attached specification, attorney docket, or title). Failure to include required information can trigger OPAP notices to supply missing parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor Citizenship Requirement (pre- and post‑Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, the citizenship of the inventor is no longer required by 35 U.S.C. 115 or 37 CFR 1.63. For nonprovisional applications filed before September 16, 2012, pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 115 requires the inventor(s) to state his or her citizenship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an inventor is not a citizen of any country, a statement to that effect satisfies the pre‑AIA requirement. Statements about 'citizenship applied for' or future citizenship do not meet the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor Residence Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor’s place of residence (city and either state or foreign country) is required to be included in a nonprovisional application for compliance with 37 CFR 1.63 unless it is included in an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An inventor in the U.S. Armed Services may provide a statement to that effect in lieu of a residence. Residence must be on the cover sheet for a provisional application unless included in an application data sheet. For change of residence, see MPEP §719.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor Mailing or Post Office Address Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor’s mailing or post office address is required to be supplied on the oath or declaration, if not stated in an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.63(b), pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.63(c), and 37 CFR 1.76).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP will notify applicant if the mailing address is omitted. 'Mailing address' means the address where the inventor customarily receives mail (home or business address or PO box); attorney's address with instruction to send communications 'in care of' attorney is insufficient. If an inventor does not execute the oath (but substitute statement under 1.64 is filed), the inventor’s most recent home address must be given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature Execution — Form and Attachment Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no requirement that a signature be made in any particular manner; titles (e.g., 'Dr.') and non‑English character signatures are acceptable; if unable to write, an inventor's mark must be attested by a witness; EFS‑Web filed applications must contain an oath/declaration personally signed by the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is improper to sign an oath/declaration that is not attached to or does not identify the application to which it is directed. 'Attached' means physically located together at the time of execution (physical fastening not required). Copies of declarations are encouraged. Notary's jurat authenticates a mark in case of oath.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual Declarations and Joint Inventors' Oaths
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 by each actual inventor must be presented. Each inventor need not execute the same oath or declaration. Where individual declarations are executed, they must be submitted as individual declarations rather than combined into one declaration (by combining the signature pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nonprovisional international design applications see 37 CFR 1.1021(d) and 1.1067. For applications filed before September 16, 2012, each oath must contain a complete listing of all inventors to indicate the appropriate inventive entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor Must Review and Understand Application and Duty of Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: An inventor must, before executing the oath or declaration, (i) review and understand the contents of the application; and (ii) be aware of his or her duty of disclosure (see 37 CFR 1.63(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If changes made to the specification before filing result in substantial alterations, the inventor may not understand the contents or be aware of the duty to disclose and should not execute the oath/declaration without review. Improper execution/filing can lead to abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who May Execute an Oath/Declaration — Post‑ and Pre‑Sept 16, 2012 Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012: only inventors can execute an oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63; the applicant may execute a substitute statement under 37 CFR 1.64 in permitted circumstances. For applications filed before September 16, 2012: pre‑AIA statutes allow joint inventors to sign for an inventor who cannot be reached or refuses to join (35 U.S.C. 116), a legal representative to sign for a deceased/incapacitated inventor (35 U.S.C. 117), and a party with proprietary interest to sign if inventor cannot be reached (35 U.S.C. 118).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An attorney may not sign on behalf of an inventor (even with power of attorney) unless he/she has a proprietary interest; precedents (Opinions/decisions) show such signatures were defective. See MPEP §§409.01–409.03 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alterations to Application Papers and Need for Re‑execution of Oath/Declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.52(c) permits interlineation, erasure, cancellation or other alteration of application papers before or after signing of the inventor's oath/declaration, provided that the statements in the inventor's oath/declaration pursuant to §1.63 remain applicable to those application papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An inventor is not required to re‑execute an oath/declaration after minor changes (e.g., typographical errors, grammatical problems, clarifying sentences). If changes would introduce new matter (i.e., would have been new matter if made to a filed application), then the inventor should execute a new oath/declaration after reviewing the amended application. A substitute specification (§1.125) may be required if application papers become non‑compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor Legal Name Requirement (post‑ and pre‑Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: For nonprovisional applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, 37 CFR 1.63 requires identification of the inventor by his or her legal name. For applications filed before September 16, 2012, pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.63(a)(2) required full name including family name and at least one given name without abbreviation together with any other given name or initial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an inventor's full given name is a singular letter (e.g., 'J. Doe' where 'J' is the full given name), identify as such and include a statement that the singular lettering is the inventor’s given name to avoid an objection. Typewritten name including middle name/initial will be used even if signature omits it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of Inventor Name
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective September 16, 2012, any request to have the name of the inventor or a joint inventor in a nonprovisional application corrected or updated (including typographical or transliteration error) must be by way of a request under 37 CFR 1.48(f) including (1) an application data sheet in accordance with 37 CFR 1.76 that identifies each inventor by his or her legal name, and (2) the processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests under 37 CFR 1.48(f) filed on or after Sept 16, 2012 are treated by OPAP; if compliant, OPAP will correct records and send a corrected filing receipt. If error is not detected until after payment of the issue fee, either (A) withdraw from issue (37 CFR 1.313(c)(2)) and submit a request under 1.48(f) with an RCE (1.114), or (B) file a certificate of correction with a petition under 1.182 after patent issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of Inventor Name After Filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective Sept 16, 2012, to change an inventor’s name after filing, submit a request under 37 CFR 1.48(f) including an application data sheet per 37 CFR 1.76 and the processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP treats requests under 1.48(f) and will correct Office records if request complies. Since amendments are not permitted after payment of issue fee (37 CFR 1.312), a request under 1.48(f) filed after payment of the issue fee cannot be granted. If application is assigned, submit corrected assignment and recording fee to Assignment Division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of Joint Inventor Names
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after Sept 16, 2012 the order of names of joint patentees in the patent heading is taken from the order in which the names appear in the application data sheet if submitted before or with the inventor's oath/declaration; for earlier applications the order is taken from the order in which the typewritten names appear in the original oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care should be exercised selecting preferred order before filing because requests to subsequently shift names require 37 CFR 1.48(f) and are treated as amendments; changes cannot be granted after payment of issue fee. OPAP will change order in Office computer records and send corrected filing receipt if 1.48(f) request granted. Suggested practice: keep typewritten and signed names in same preferred order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the Application in the Oath/Declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.63 requires that an oath or declaration identify the application (e.g., specification and drawings) to which it is directed. The following combinations supplied in an oath/declaration filed on the application filing date are acceptable minimums for identifying the application: (A) name of inventor(s) and reference to an attached specification/application; (B) name of inventor(s) and attorney docket number on the specification; or (C) name of inventor(s) and title of the invention on the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For oaths/declarations filed after the filing date, acceptable identification includes: (A) application number (series code + serial number); (B) serial number and filing date; (C) international application number; (D) international registration number of an international design application; (E) attorney docket number as filed; (F) title of the invention on the specification plus reference to an attached specification/application; or (G) title plus a cover letter accurately identifying the application by application number or serial number and filing date. Absent statements to the contrary, PTO will presume the executed oath/declaration corresponds to the application filed in the USPTO. An oath attached to a cover letter referencing an incorrect application may not become associated with the correct application and could result in abandonment. Variances require petition under 37 CFR 1.183 with fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Inventorship — Who May Be Named and Contribution Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When an invention is made by two or more persons jointly, they shall apply for patent jointly and each make the required oath. Inventors may apply jointly even though (1) they did not physically work together or at the same time, (2) each did not make the same type or amount of contribution, or (3) each did not make a contribution to the subject matter of every claim of the patent (35 U.S.C. 116 and 37 CFR 1.45).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple inventors are named in a nonprovisional application, each named inventor must have made a contribution, individually or jointly, to the subject matter of at least one claim. For provisional applications, each named inventor must have made a contribution to the subject matter disclosed. The examiner should assume common ownership of claimed subject matter unless evidence indicates otherwise; correction of inventorship may be required under 37 CFR 1.48 when claims are amended so that named inventors no longer correspond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omitted Inventor and Correction of Errors in Inventorship
rubrics_metrics.description: If through error a person is named as inventor or an inventor is omitted, the Director may permit the application to be amended accordingly under terms he prescribes (35 U.S.C. 116, pre‑AIA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a joint inventor refuses to join or cannot be reached after diligent effort, the other inventor(s) may file on behalf of both and the Director, on proof and after prescribed notice, may grant a patent subject to the omitted inventor's rights; the omitted inventor may later join. Applicants are responsible for correcting inventorship in compliance with 37 CFR 1.48 when claims are amended to change inventorship. 37 CFR 1.48 permits correction where the correct inventor(s) were disclosed in the application as filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Oath or Declaration (37 CFR 1.67)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may submit a supplemental inventor's oath or declaration meeting the requirements of §1.63, §1.64, or §1.162 to correct any deficiencies or inaccuracies present in an earlier-filed inventor's oath or declaration (37 CFR 1.67).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental oath/declaration must be executed by the person whose oath/declaration is being withdrawn, replaced, or corrected. Deficiencies due to failure to meet §1.63(b) may be corrected with an application data sheet per §1.76, except that any correction of inventorship must be pursuant to §1.48. The Office will not require an additional inventor's oath/declaration from a person who has already executed one in compliance with 35 U.S.C. 115 and §1.63 or 1.162. No new matter may be introduced into a nonprovisional application by filing a supplemental oath/declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuations/Divisionals When a Petition Under 37 CFR 1.48 Was Filed in Prior Application
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional application of a prior application in which a petition (or request) under 37 CFR 1.48 to add any of the inventors was filed should be filed with a copy of an executed declaration naming the correct inventive entity from the prior application or a newly executed declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of any decision under 37 CFR 1.48 from the prior application is not required to be filed in the continuation or divisional application. See MPEP §602.01(c)(3) for pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.48 language. This is distinct from the 1.47 decision situation described elsewhere; follow the specific instructions for the relevant rule.
